title: 식품 업계의 기만적인 건강 주장
exam: EBS 올림포스 독해의 기본 2 (2025) 서논술형 논술형
fullPassage: The ingenuity of the food industry is demonstrated by its ability to simultaneously design and market new products that appeal to consumers who want both "good-for-you" and diet foods. By offering one product line that profits by producing obesity and another that generates revenues by claiming to reduce weight, food companies have found a way to have their cake and eat it, too. In these "healthier" products, food companies remove some of the calories, sugars, fats, and salt added to "fun-to-eat foods" in order to address consumers' concerns about health. Others simply add nutrients to the same unhealthy product. For example, cereal companies simply add vitamins A, C, or iron to sweetened refined-grain products, then label them as "healthy," rather than using the whole grains recommended for healthier diets. In 2009, 86 percent of cereal marketed to children contained mostly refined grain.
